A 30-Day Adventure Through the Old Testament

A Note for Parents


Have you ever tried to explain the Old Testament to a child? It can be tricky. There are rules about food. There are rules about clothes. There are rules about a big tent. It can seem strange and confusing.


But here is the secret. The Old Testament is not just a list of weird rules. It is a treasure map. Every rule, every tent, every ceremony is a clue. They all point to one person. That person is Jesus.


This book is a 30 day adventure for you and your kids. Each day has a short story. Each day has a fun activity. Each day has a simple prayer. Each day has a coloring page. You do not need to be a Bible expert to lead this. You just need to be willing to explore with your kids. Get ready to pitch a tent. Get ready to find some clues. Get ready to find Jesus.


How to Use This Book


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 5 to 10 minutes. Read the secret clue. Read the big reveal. Do the family activity together. Say the prayer out loud. Let your child color the picture. The goal is not perfection. The goal is connection. Have fun with it. Get messy. Ask questions. Laugh together. This is an adventure. Let us begin.


---

pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle." - Exodus 40:34


God told Moses to build a special tent. It was called the tabernacle. It was not a normal tent. It was a holy tent. It was where God met with His people. The cloud of God's glory filled the tent. God lived in a tent with His people. That is a strange clue. Why would God live in a tent?


The Big Reveal
"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


The tent was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the new tent. He is God living with us. He is God in the flesh. He came to be with us. He came to live among us. The big tent was a picture of Jesus.


Family Activity
Build a blanket fort in your living room. Crawl inside with your child. Read the story of the tabernacle. Talk about how God wanted to be close to His people. Talk about how Jesus came to be close to us. Sit in the fort and say, "God is with us."


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, God, for wanting to be close to me. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you for living in my heart. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A big colorful tent with a cloud of glory above it.

pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"These are the commands, decrees and laws the LORD your God directed me to teach you to observe." - Deuteronomy 6:1


God gave His people many rules. There were rules about food. There were rules about clothes. There were rules about washing. There were rules about farming. There were lots of rules. Some of them seem weird to us. Why did God give so many rules?


The Big Reveal
"For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ." - John 1:17


The rules were a clue. They pointed to Jesus. The rules showed the people what was right. But they could not make the people right. The rules showed the people they needed a savior. Jesus is the one who makes us right. Jesus is the fulfillment of the rules.


Family Activity
Play a game of "Simon Says." Give your child lots of rules to follow. Then tell them the game is over. Talk about how hard it is to follow all the rules. Talk about how Jesus kept all the rules for us. Jesus is our helper.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for keeping the rules for me. Thank you for being my helper. Thank you for your grace. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt

pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old." - Exodus 12:5


God told His people to bring a lamb. The lamb had to be perfect. It could not have any spots. It could not have any broken bones. It could not have any sickness. It had to be the best lamb. Why did the lamb have to be perfect?


The Big Reveal
"Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" - John 1:29


The perfect lamb was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the perfect Lamb of God. He is without spot. He is without sin. He is perfect. He gave His life for us. The perfect lamb was a picture of Jesus.


Family Activity
Draw a picture of a lamb. Add a big red heart on the lamb. Talk about how Jesus is the perfect Lamb. Talk about how He loves us. Sing "Mary Had a Little Lamb" and change the words to talk about Jesus.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the perfect Lamb. Thank you for taking away my sin. Thank you for loving me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt

pages.title: Day 3: The Lamb Without a Spot

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you." - Exodus 12:13


God told His people to kill a lamb. They had to take the blood. They had to paint it on their doors. The blood was a sign. When the angel of death came, he would see the blood. He would pass over that house. The people inside would be safe. Why did they need the blood?


The Big Reveal
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


The red door was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is our Passover Lamb. He shed His blood for us. His blood is on the door of our hearts. When judgment comes, it passes over us. We are safe because of the blood of Jesus.


Family Activity
Cut out a paper door. Color it red. Tape it to your child's bedroom door. Talk about how the blood of the lamb saved the people. Talk about how the blood of Jesus saves us. Every time you see the door, say, "Jesus saves me."


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for your blood. Thank you for saving me. Thank you for protecting me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A door painted with a red stripe.
pages.title: Day 4: The Red Door

pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast." - Exodus 12:15


God told His people to eat a special bread. It was called unleavened bread. It was bread without yeast. It was flat and hard. It was quick to make. Yeast makes bread puffy and big. But God said, "No yeast. Not today." Why did God care about yeast?


The Big Reveal
"Therefore let us keep the Festival, not with the old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the bread of sincerity and truth." - 1 Corinthians 5:8


The bread without yeast was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Yeast is a picture of sin. It spreads and puffs up. Jesus is the bread without yeast. He is the Bread of Life. He has no sin. He is pure. He is the true bread from heaven.


Family Activity
Bake a simple flatbread together. Or buy some pita bread. Talk about how the bread is flat because it has no yeast. Talk about how Jesus is pure like the flatbread. Jesus is the Bread of Life.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the Bread of Life. Thank you for being pure. Thank you for being without sin. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A round loaf of flatbread with a big smile.
pages.title: Day 5: The Bread Without Yeast

The Secret Clue
"Eat the meat roasted over the fire, along with bitter herbs." - Exodus 12:8


God told His people to eat bitter herbs. Bitter herbs are plants that taste yucky. They are not sweet. They are not yummy. They remind you of sad things. They reminded the people of their slavery. They reminded them of their pain. Why did God tell them to eat something bitter?


The Big Reveal
"He was pierced for our transgressions, he was crushed for our iniquities." - Isaiah 53:5


The bitter herbs were a clue. They pointed to Jesus. Jesus experienced bitter things. He was pierced. He was crushed. He was hurt. He took the pain for us. He took the sadness for us. Jesus understands our pain.


Family Activity
Taste a lemon or a piece of dark chocolate. Talk about how it tastes bitter. Talk about how Jesus experienced pain for us. Talk about how Jesus understands when we are sad. He is with us in our sad times.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for understanding my pain. Thank you for taking my sadness. Thank you for being with me. I love you. Amen."

The Secret Clue
"This is how you are to eat it: with your cloak tucked into your belt, your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand." - Exodus 12:11


God told His people to eat the Passover meal with their shoes on. They had to be ready. They had to be prepared. They had to be ready to go. They were about to leave Egypt. They were about to go on a journey. They had to be ready to move.


The Big Reveal
"So you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him." - Matthew 24:44


The shoes were a clue. They pointed to Jesus. Jesus calls us to be ready. He is coming back. He wants us to be prepared. He wants us to be watching. He wants us to be ready to go with Him. The shoes were a picture of readiness.


Family Activity
Put on your shoes. Run around the room. Talk about how the people had to be ready to leave Egypt. Talk about how we need to be ready for Jesus to come back. We need to be ready. We need to be watching.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my guide. Help me to be ready for you. Help me to be watching. I love you. Amen."

God told His people to hold a staff. A staff is a walking stick. It is a tool. It is a guide. It helps you walk. It helps you stay steady. It helps you go in the right direction. They held the staff because they were going on a journey. They needed help.


The Big Reveal
"I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." - John 10:11


The staff was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the Good Shepherd. He is our guide. He is our help. He leads us. He protects us. He guides us. We can hold onto Him. He is our staff.

Kid's Prayer

The Secret Clue
"It is a night of watching for the LORD, to bring them out of Egypt." - Exodus 12:42


The night of the Passover was a night of watching. The people were awake. The people were waiting. The people were watching. They were waiting for God to deliver them. They were waiting for God to save them. It was a night of anticipation.


The Big Reveal
"So be on your guard! Remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears." - Acts 20:31


The night of watching was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the one we watch for. He is the one we wait for. He is coming back. We need to be on our guard. We need to be watching. We need to be ready.


Family Activity
Turn off the lights. Turn on a flashlight. Play a game of "I Spy" in the dark. Talk about how the people were watching on the night of the Passover. Talk about how we watch for Jesus. He is coming back. We need to be watching.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the one I watch for. Help me to be on my guard. Help me to be watching. I love you. Amen."

The Secret Clue
"This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD—a lasting ordinance." - Exodus 12:14


God told His people to remember. He told them to remember the Passover. He told them to remember what He had done. He told them to remember the day of deliverance. He told them to celebrate it every year. It was a memorial. It was a reminder.


The Big Reveal
"Do this in remembrance of me." - 1 Corinthians 11:24


The memorial was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus gave us a memorial. He gave us communion. He gave us the bread and the cup. He said, "Do this in remembrance of me." We remember what Jesus did. We remember His sacrifice. We remember His love.


Family Activity

Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for remembering me. Help me to remember you. Help me to remember your sacrifice. Help me to remember your love. I love you. Amen."

The Secret Clue
"Celebrate this day as a lasting ordinance for the generations to come." - Exodus 12:17


God told His people to tell their children. They were to tell their children about the Passover. They were to tell their grandchildren. They were to tell the next generation. They were to tell the story. They were to pass it down. It was a story of deliverance. It was a story of grace.


The Big Reveal
"We will not hide them from their descendants; we will tell the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of the LORD, his power, and the wonders he has done." - Psalm 78:4


The generations were a clue. They pointed to Jesus. We are to tell the next generation about Jesus. We are to tell them about His love. We are to tell them about His sacrifice. We are to tell them about His grace. We are to pass it down.


Family Activity
Draw a picture of your family tree. Talk about the people in your family who love Jesus. Talk about how you can tell your children and grandchildren about Jesus. You can pass down the story.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for my family. Thank you for the people who told me about you. Help me to tell others about you. I love you. Amen."

pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"When the LORD goes through the land to strike down the Egyptians, he will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway, and he will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses." - Exodus 12:23


The destroyer was coming. The destroyer was passing through. The destroyer was bringing judgment. But the blood was a sign. The blood was a protection. The blood stopped the destroyer. The blood saved the people.


The Big Reveal
"And having disarmed the powers and authorities, he made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross." - Colossians 2:15


The destroyer was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus stopped the destroyer. He disarmed the powers. He triumphed over the authorities. He defeated the enemy. He protected us. He saved us.


Family Activity
Play a game of "freeze tag." One person is the "destroyer." They try to tag the others. The others can be saved by touching a "safe base." Talk about how Jesus is our safe base. He protects us from the destroyer. He saves us.


Kid's Prayer

"On the first day hold a sacred assembly, and another one on the seventh day. Do no work at all on these days, except to prepare food for everyone to eat; that is all you may do." - Exodus 12:16


The first day and the seventh day were special. They were sacred assemblies. They were days of rest. They were days of worship. They were days of gathering. The people gathered together. They worshipped together. They rested together.


The Big Reveal
"There remains, then, a Sabbath-rest for the people of God; for anyone who enters God's rest also rests from their works, just as God did from his." - Hebrews 4:9-10


The first and seventh day were clues. They pointed to Jesus. Jesus is our rest. He is our worship. He is our gathering. He is the one we rest in. He is the one we worship. He is the one we gather around.

"If any household is too small for a whole lamb, they must share one with their neighbors who live nearby, having regard for the number of people." - Exodus 12:4


The lamb was for the household. It was for the family. It was for the neighbors. It was for the community. It was to be shared. It was to be eaten together. The people were not alone. They were together.


The Big Reveal
"They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer." - Acts 2:42


The lamb for the household was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the lamb for the household. He is the lamb for the family. He is the lamb for the community. He is the lamb we share. He is the lamb we eat together. He is the lamb we celebrate together.


Family Activity

Talk about a time you were in trouble. Talk about how someone helped you. Talk about how Jesus helps us. He takes our punishment. He saves us. He loves us.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for saving me from judgment. Thank you for taking my punishment. Thank you for your love. I love you. Amen."

pages.title: Day 23: The Plague Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD—a lasting ordinance." - Exodus 12:14


The Passover was a feast. It was a celebration. It was a festival. It was a time of joy. It was a time of gratitude. It was a time of remembrance. The people celebrated what God had done. They celebrated their deliverance.


The Big Reveal
"Let us rejoice and be glad and give him glory! For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready." - Revelation 19:7


The feast was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the feast. He is the celebration. He is the festival. He is the wedding of the Lamb. We will celebrate with Him forever. We will feast with Him forever.


Family Activity
Have a family feast. Make a special meal. Set the table. Light candles. Talk about how Jesus is the reason we celebrate. Talk about how one day we will feast with Him in heaven. It will be the greatest feast ever.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the feast. Thank you for being the celebration. Thank you for the joy. I love you. Amen."

pages.title: Day 24: The Feast Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD—a lasting ordinance." - Exodus 12:14


The Passover was a memorial. It was a remembrance. It was a reminder. It was a reminder of what God had done. It was a reminder of deliverance. It was a reminder of grace. The people remembered. They remembered God's love.


The Big Reveal
"Do this in remembrance of me." - 1 Corinthians 11:24


The memorial was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus gave us a memorial. He gave us communion. He said, "Do this in remembrance of me." We remember what Jesus did. We remember His sacrifice. We remember His love. We remember Him.


Family Activity
Make a special memory box. Put things in it that remind you of God's goodness. A picture. A note. A small toy. Talk about how the people remembered the Passover. Talk about how we remember Jesus. We remember His love.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for remembering me. Help me to remember you. Help me to remember your sacrifice. Help me to remember your love. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A heart with a cross and a smile inside it.
pages.title: Day 25: The Memorial Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"On the first day hold a sacred assembly, and another one on the seventh day. Do no work at all on these days, except to prepare food for everyone to eat; that is all you may do." - Exodus 12:16


The first day and the seventh day were special. They were sacred assemblies. They were days of rest. They were days of worship. They were days of gathering. The people gathered together. They worshipped together. They rested together.


The Big Reveal
"There remains, then, a Sabbath-rest for the people of God; for anyone who enters God's rest also rests from their works, just as God did from his." - Hebrews 4:9-10


The first and seventh day were clues. They pointed to Jesus. Jesus is our rest. He is our worship. He is our gathering. He is the one we rest in. He is the one we worship. He is the one we gather around.


Family Activity
Have a day of rest. Take a nap. Read a book. Go for a walk. Talk about how God wants us to rest. Talk about how Jesus is our rest. We can rest in Him. We can trust Him. We can worship Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my rest. Thank you for being my worship. Thank you for being my gathering. Help me to rest in you. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A person sleeping peacefully with a cross and a big smile.
pages.title: Day 26: The First and Seventh Day Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"If any household is too small for a whole lamb, they must share one with their neighbors who live nearby, having regard for the number of people." - Exodus 12:4


The lamb was for the household. It was for the family. It was for the neighbors. It was for the community. It was to be shared. It was to be eaten together. The people were not alone. They were together.


The Big Reveal
"They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer." - Acts 2:42


The lamb for the household was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the lamb for the household. He is the lamb for the family. He is the lamb for the community. He is the lamb we share. He is the lamb we eat together. He is the lamb we celebrate together.


Family Activity
Invite a friend or a neighbor over for dinner. Share a meal. Talk about how the lamb was shared with neighbors. Talk about how Jesus is shared with others. We can share Jesus. We can share His love. We can share His grace.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the lamb for the household. Thank you for my family. Thank you for my friends. Help me to share you with others. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A table with a lamb, a cross, and a big heart.
pages.title: Day 27: The Lamb for the Household Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"Then they are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs." - Exodus 12:7


The blood was on the doorframe. It was on the sides. It was on the top. It was a sign. It was a protection. It was a covering. The people were safe because of the blood. The people were saved because of the blood.


The Big Reveal
"In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of God's grace." - Ephesians 1:7


The blood on the doorframe was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus shed His blood for us. His blood is on the door of our hearts. His blood is our protection. His blood is our covering. His blood is our redemption. His blood is our salvation.


Family Activity
Draw a picture of a door. Color it red. Write "Jesus" on the door. Talk about how the blood of the lamb was on the door. Talk about how the blood of Jesus is on our hearts. We are safe because of the blood.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for your blood. Thank you for protecting me. Thank you for covering me. Thank you for saving me. I love you. Amen."

A door with a red heart and a cross on it.
pages.title: Day 28: The Blood on the Doorframe Again

pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"It is the LORD's Passover." - Exodus 12:11


The Passover was the Lord's. It was His. It was His celebration. It was His memorial. It was His story. It was His deliverance. It was His love. It was His grace.


The Big Reveal
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


The Lord's Passover was a clue. It pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the Lord's Passover. He is the celebration. He is the memorial. He is the story. He is the deliverance. He is the love. He is the grace.


Family Activity
Sing a song about Jesus. Dance around the room. Talk about how Jesus is the reason we celebrate. Talk about how Jesus is the reason we sing. We celebrate Him. We sing to Him. We love Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the Lord's Passover. Thank you for being the celebration. Thank you for being the story. I love you. Amen."

pages.title: Day 29: The Lord's Passover Again

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Secret Clue
"It is the LORD's Passover." - Exodus 12:11


The Passover was a shadow. It was a symbol. It was a ceremony. It was pointing to something greater. It was pointing to someone greater. It was pointing to Jesus.


The Big Reveal
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed. Therefore let us keep the Festival..." - 1 Corinthians 5:7-8


Jesus is the real meaning. He is the Passover lamb. He is the sacrifice. He is the fulfillment of the ceremony. He is the real meaning of the Passover. He is the reason we celebrate. He is the reason we remember. He is the reason we have hope.


Family Activity
Have a celebration. Make a special treat. Light a candle. Talk about how Jesus is the real meaning of the Passover. Talk about how Jesus is the reason we have hope. We celebrate Jesus. We love Jesus. We thank Jesus.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the real meaning of the Passover. Thank you for being the Passover lamb. Thank you for being the sacrifice. Thank you for being the fulfillment of the ceremony. Help me to live in the reality. Help me to live in you. I love you. Amen."

A Note for the Parent: Building on the Foundation


You did it. You spent 30 days walking your children through the big tent and the special rules. But the adventure does not end here. It is just beginning.


Here are a few tips to keep going:


1. Make it a habit, not a chore. Do not stress about reading the Bible for 30 minutes a day. A simple 5 minute rhythm before bed is better than an hour once a month.
2. Let them see you reading. Kids do what they see. Let them catch you reading your Bible. Let them see that it matters to you.
3. Ask "Where is Jesus?" in every story. Whenever you read a Bible story, ask your child, "Where do you see Jesus in this story?" This trains them to look for Jesus everywhere.
4. Recommended next steps. Read The Jesus Storybook Bible by Sally Lloyd-Jones. Read The Biggest Story by Kevin DeYoung. Keep pointing them to the Treasure.


You are doing a great job. Keep going.
